panels.prompt: Opening visual trick at night: an immense aerial view of a luminous city grid seen from high above, orderly blocks and streets stretching to the horizon, cool blue-white light with a few violet and green districts. The camera is in the middle of pulling back, and the edges of the frame reveal that this city is actually a stylized top-down view of a tiny chip package on a workbench under a warm desk lamp. The transition from aerial city to physical chip is visually unmistakable. In the real-world foreground, Kai holds an opened generic smartphone and Lin stands beside him at the desk. No real brands. The city is clearly an explanatory visualization, not a physical city built on the chip.

Night at a workbench under a warm desk lamp. Kai taps the screen of a generic smartphone; at the instant his fingertip makes contact, a single narrow cold blue-white ribbon of light emerges from his fingertip and dives into the phone, visualizing the electrical signal from this one tap. Lin raises her LEFT wrist and her round black watch emits its first concentric amber ruler-tick ripple, with no numbers. Kai leans toward the phone, surprised and curious. Opened old phone and a small unmarked black chip package rest nearby. The light trail is the story's guide, not a decorative circuit pattern.

The signature shrinking journey at macro scale: Lin and Kai, now tiny, descend toward a phone motherboard while concentric amber ruler-tick ripples contract around them. A single rice grain towers beside Kai like a massive boulder; farther ahead, one human hair stretches across the scene like a gigantic vertical cliff with visible cuticle texture. A narrow cold blue-white light ribbon leads them downward. Kai flails in astonishment, Lin remains calm and points toward the guide light. Strong scale comparison, low wide-angle macro shot, physically plausible rice and hair, no dust shaped like circuits.

Exploded-view explanatory visualization of a generic modern fan-out phone chip package at night, with no brand-specific design. From bottom to top: green motherboard, a grid of large silver solder balls, one very thin redistribution wiring layer with fine copper paths, and a thin opaque grey silicon die. The silicon die's active face points DOWN toward the redistribution layer and motherboard. No thick organic package substrate and no row of large copper C4 bumps. The silicon die is suspended in mid-air and beginning to rotate face-up purely as an explanatory visualization, with thin white cut-edge light. Lin gestures toward the active face, Kai watches in surprise. A separate thin memory package may hover above the processor, showing that a real package can contain more than one die.

A single enhancement-mode N-channel gate-all-around nanosheet transistor in the OFF state, shown as a precise cinematic cutaway. Three thin grey silicon nanosheets run straight between source and drain blocks, each wrapped on all four sides by a very thin pale insulating layer and dark steel-grey gate metal. The silicon sheets are dim: there is no continuous population of amber electron specks joining source to drain, only a few isolated specks inside the silicon and empty gaps along the path. The gate is not glowing. Kai examines the interrupted path with curiosity; Lin points to the gate from the side. No copper wires or vias below the transistor, no light channels in the gaps, no moving parts.

The same enhancement-mode N-channel gate-all-around nanosheet transistor now switching ON, identical camera and structure to an OFF-state comparison. Three thin grey silicon nanosheets connect source and drain, each surrounded by a very thin pale insulating layer and dark gate metal. The gate glows gently. Warm amber electron specks gather INSIDE each silicon sheet close to the insulating layer and form one continuous luminous channel through every sheet from source to drain. No electrons travel through the insulating layer and no light channel floats in the gaps. Lin and Kai stand at the edge, small against the structure, watching the channel form. No mechanical gate movement, no copper wires below.

Wide cinematic pull-back above a vast regular array of gate-all-around transistors. A cold blue-white signal ribbon reaches one transistor; its gate lights gently and an amber channel forms inside its silicon nanosheets, then the signal continues to the next gate. A sequence of neighboring transistors lights in order, illustrating signals propagating through logic circuits rather than electrons flying across the chip. Lin and Kai stand on a transistor in the foreground, dwarfed by the array extending to the horizon. Lin faces the camera almost squarely. Her anatomical LEFT arm is on the viewer's RIGHT side of her torso: she extends that LEFT hand toward the signal, and her round black watch is clearly visible on that extended LEFT wrist. Her anatomical RIGHT arm is on the viewer's LEFT side of her torso: that RIGHT arm hangs naturally at her side, and that RIGHT wrist is completely bare, with NO watch, NO band and NO jewelry. The only watch is on the pointing LEFT wrist on the viewer's RIGHT, never on the hanging RIGHT wrist on the viewer's LEFT. No paired inverter or special two-device grouping is needed in this image; the inverter will be explained by a separate circuit overlay. No decorative glowing circuit traces on empty surfaces.
